---
title: "Seasonal stage x Bd modeling"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
df-print: kable
---

Purpose: per-species Bayesian models of how the subadult - adult difference in *Bd* infection
changes through the season (stage x season), following the glmmTMB screen in
`01_season_screen.Rmd`.

Design decisions (see the screen and brainstorm):

- **No weather terms.** Within temperate species, 30-day temperature is largely seasonal, so
  stage x season and stage x temperature cannot be separated. The seasonal curves here therefore
  include whatever climate comes with the season. The unified model keeps weather for its own
  purpose (adjusting the overall subadult - adult contrast).
- **One model per species**, for the species with enough co-sampling of both life stages:
  *A. canorus* and five ranids. The two-window Panamanian species (*Colostethus*,
  *L. warszewitschii*) are dropped: their life stages are mostly sampled in different windows.
- **Same random-effect structure as the GAM models**, so differences from them come from the
  seasonal terms, not the random effects.

Production fits run on the cluster with `r-brms-contained/size_bd_season_modeling.R` (same data
prep, formula, priors and settings; `hpc/run_size_bd_season_modeling.sbatch` fits each species as
an array task). Keep the two in sync.

Run order: needs the unified model data from `size_bd_unified/01_model_data.Rmd` (the same file
model m11g was fit to).

# Setup

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| output: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show setup code"

librarian::shelf(tidyverse, here, brms, cmdstanr, patchwork)

models_dir = here("size_bd_season", "models")
dir.create(models_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

load(here("size_bd_unified", "intermediates", "bd_model_env_unified_2026-11-12.RData"))

```

# Data
```{r}
# species with enough co-sampled weeks of both life stages (screen tier 1, 10 / 6), minus the
# two-window panamanian species. alphabetical order = cluster array index (0-5)
season_species = c("anaxyrus_canorus",
                   "rana_cascadae",
                   "rana_catesbeiana",
                   "rana_clamitans",
                   "rana_muscosa",
                   "rana_sierrae")

# season covariate: months from july 1 (day 182). centering and scaling only changes the units
# of the smooth's linear (unpenalized) part, which makes its prior easier to set: a slope of 1
# means a change of 1 on the logit (hu) or log (mu) scale per month.
prep_season_data = function(brms_data, species_name) {
  brms_data %>%
    filter(taxon_capture == species_name) %>%
    mutate(life_stage_simple = factor(life_stage_simple, levels = c("adult", "subadult")),
           doy = as.integer(format(date, "%j")),
           season_m = (doy - 182) / 30.44) %>%
    # drop unused levels so random-effect terms have no empty columns
    droplevels()
}

season_data = purrr::map(set_names(season_species), ~ prep_season_data(brms_data, .x))

# sample sizes per species and stage
map_dfr(season_data, ~ count(.x, life_stage_simple), .id = "taxon_capture") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = life_stage_simple, values_from = n)

```

# Model structure
```{r}

set_cmdstan_path(Sys.getenv("cmd_stan_path"))

# for both the load part (mu, log scale, Bd-positive swabs) and the detection part (hu, logit
# scale of non-detection):
#   1 + life_stage_simple            stage intercepts (adult reference)
#   s(season_m, by = life_stage_simple, k = 5)
#                                    a separate seasonal curve per stage. a thin-plate spline,
#                                    not cyclic: most species cover only part of the year, so the
#                                    curve is a within-season shape, not a full annual cycle.
#                                    k = 5 allows one dip-and-recovery (e.g. r. cascadae) without
#                                    much wiggle. the subadult - adult contrast at a date is the
#                                    gap between the two curves.
#   (1 | population:life_stage_simple)
#                                    population effects, separate by stage (as in unified / gam)
#   (0 + life_stage_simple | population:year)
#                                    population-year effects, correlated between stages
# sigma ~ 1 + (1 | population)       residual spread of log load varies by population (as in gam)
season_formula = bf(
  bd_load_co100_density ~ 1 + life_stage_simple +
    s(season_m, by = life_stage_simple, k = 5) +
    (1 | population:life_stage_simple) +
    (0 + life_stage_simple | population:year),

  hu ~ 1 + life_stage_simple +
    s(season_m, by = life_stage_simple, k = 5) +
    (1 | population:life_stage_simple) +
    (0 + life_stage_simple | population:year),

  sigma ~ 1 + (1 | population)
)

# priors, on the same scales as the unified model (m11g). classes:
#   Intercept:  intercept (adult, at the centered predictors)
#   b:          the subadult offset AND the linear (unpenalized) part of each seasonal smooth
#               (coef "sseason_m:life_stage_simple<stage>_1", per month). the class-wide b prior
#               covers the subadult offset; the smooths' linear parts get their own prior by coef
#   sds:        how wiggly each smooth may be. the brms default here is student_t(3, 0, 6)
#               (scaled from the data), which allows very wiggly curves, especially on the logit
#               (hu) scale; student_t(3, 0, 2.5) is moderately regularizing but still allows
#               rises of several log units (e.g. r. sierrae subadult load)
#   sd:         random-effect sds
season_priors = c(
  # mu: log load density among positives
  prior(normal(5, 4), class = "Intercept"),
  prior(normal(0, 3), class = "b"),                                              # subadult offset
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "sseason_m:life_stage_simpleadult_1"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "sseason_m:life_stage_simplesubadult_1"),
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 2.5), class = "sds"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sd"),

  # hu: logit of non-detection
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "Intercept", dpar = "hu"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", dpar = "hu"),                                 # subadult offset
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "sseason_m:life_stage_simpleadult_1", dpar = "hu"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "sseason_m:life_stage_simplesubadult_1", dpar = "hu"),
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 2.5), class = "sds", dpar = "hu"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sd", dpar = "hu"),

  # sigma: log residual sd of log load
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = "Intercept", dpar = "sigma"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sd", dpar = "sigma")
)

# validate_prior errors if any prior does not match a model parameter, and shows the full prior
# set (ours, plus brms defaults for anything not set, e.g. the lkj(1) prior on the adult /
# subadult population-year correlation). the coef names come from the stage levels, so they are
# the same for every species; checking one species is enough.
validate_prior(season_priors,
               formula = season_formula,
               data = season_data[["anaxyrus_canorus"]],
               family = hurdle_lognormal())

```

# Local timing test
```{r}
#| eval: false

# short run of the real model, to estimate cluster run time and memory. warmup = 300 clears
# stan's adaptation threshold (below ~150-200 warmup the adaptation schedule is compressed and
# timing is not representative, see r-brms-contained/hpc/timing_probe.sbatch).
#
# extrapolating: sampling time scales roughly linearly with post-warmup iterations, warmup less
# predictably (step size adapts). the estimate below scales the slowest chain's warmup by
# 2000 / 300 and its sampling by 2000 / 100 (production: 2000 warmup + 2000 sampling; chains run
# in parallel, so the slowest chain sets the wall time). treat it as an order of magnitude, and
# compare species to see how time grows with n.
timing_species = c("anaxyrus_canorus", "rana_cascadae", "rana_sierrae")   # n ~1k, ~3.4k, ~26.5k

timing_results = map_dfr(timing_species, function(spp) {
  start = Sys.time()
  fit = brm(
    formula = season_formula,
    data = season_data[[spp]],
    family = hurdle_lognormal(),
    prior = season_priors,
    control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 12),
    chains = 4, iter = 400, warmup = 300,
    seed = 127, cores = 4, backend = "cmdstanr",
    refresh = 0
  )
  elapsed = as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), start, units = "mins"))

  # per-chain warmup / sampling seconds from stan (excludes compilation)
  chain_times = rstan::get_elapsed_time(fit$fit)

  tibble(taxon_capture = spp,
         n = nrow(season_data[[spp]]),
         total_min = elapsed,                                 # includes compilation (~1 min)
         max_chain_warmup_s = max(chain_times[, "warmup"]),
         max_chain_sample_s = max(chain_times[, "sample"]),
         # production estimate: warmup scaled 2000/300, sampling scaled 2000/100
         est_production_h = (max(chain_times[, "warmup"]) * 2000 / 300 +
                               max(chain_times[, "sample"]) * 2000 / 100) / 3600,
         divergences = sum(nuts_params(fit) %>% filter(Parameter == "divergent__") %>% pull(Value)))
})

timing_results

```

# Model fitting
```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show model fitting code"

# production fits run on the cluster (r-brms-contained/hpc/run_size_bd_season_modeling.sbatch).
# this local version is for reference or a single small species.
fit_season_model = function(spp) {
  fit = brm(
    formula = season_formula,
    data = season_data[[spp]],
    family = hurdle_lognormal(),
    prior = season_priors,
    control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 12),
    chains = 4, iter = 4000, warmup = 2000,
    seed = 127, cores = 4, backend = "cmdstanr"
  )

  fit = add_criterion(fit, "loo")
  saveRDS(fit, file.path(models_dir, paste0("size_bd_season_model_zln_s1_", spp, ".rds")))
  fit
}

# e.g. fit_season_model("anaxyrus_canorus")

```

# Load fitted models
```{r}

# cluster fits are copied into size_bd_season/models/ (named as in fit_season_model)
season_models = purrr::map(set_names(season_species), function(spp) {
  readRDS(file.path(models_dir, paste0("size_bd_season_model_zln_s1_", spp, ".rds")))
})

```

# Model checks

Checks run in order of "can we trust the sampler" -> "does the model reproduce the data" ->
"how much do the priors drive the result". Fix problems at an earlier step before reading the
later ones: a model with divergences or low ESS can't be judged on its predictive checks.

## Convergence
```{r}
# one row per species. what to look for:
#   max_rhat          < 1.01. rhat compares between- and within-chain variance; above 1.01 the
#                     chains have not mixed (they disagree about the posterior)
#   min_ess_bulk/tail > ~400 (100 per chain). effective sample size: the number of independent
#                     draws the autocorrelated chains are worth. bulk = centre of the
#                     distribution (medians), tail = 5% / 95% quantiles (intervals)
#   n_divergent       0 ideally; a handful at adapt_delta 0.95 is usually tolerable, many means
#                     the sampler cannot explore part of the posterior (often a funnel in a
#                     random-effect sd) and the estimates there may be biased
#   n_max_treedepth   iterations that hit max_treedepth (12). this is an efficiency warning,
#                     not a validity one: the sampler stopped a trajectory early
#   min_ebfmi         > 0.3. energy bfmi: low values mean the sampler moves slowly between
#                     levels of the posterior (again, often hierarchical sds)
# posterior::summarise_draws runs over every parameter, including each population-year effect,
# so the minima / maxima flag the worst-behaved parameter. this takes a minute for r. sierrae.
max_treedepth = 12   # as fit (see the fitting chunk and the cluster script)

conv_check = function(fit) {
  np = nuts_params(fit)
  dr = posterior::summarise_draws(posterior::as_draws_df(fit),
                                  posterior::default_convergence_measures())
  tibble(n_obs = nrow(fit$data),
         max_rhat = max(dr$rhat, na.rm = TRUE),
         worst_rhat_par = dr$variable[which.max(dr$rhat)],
         min_ess_bulk = min(dr$ess_bulk, na.rm = TRUE),
         min_ess_tail = min(dr$ess_tail, na.rm = TRUE),
         n_divergent = sum(np$Value[np$Parameter == "divergent__"]),
         n_max_treedepth = sum(np$Value[np$Parameter == "treedepth__"] >= max_treedepth),
         # per-chain e-bfmi; brms converts cmdstanr output to a stanfit, so rstan can read it
         min_ebfmi = min(rstan::get_bfmi(fit$fit)))
}

convergence = map_dfr(season_models, conv_check, .id = "taxon_capture")
convergence

```

## LOO / Pareto k
```{r}
# psis-loo was added on the cluster. each observation gets a pareto k, which says how well
# importance sampling approximates leaving that observation out:
#   k < 0.7  reliable
#   k > 0.7  unreliable for that point: it is very influential (often an outlying load, or the
#            only swab in a population-year). a few are common in hierarchical models with
#            many small groups; many (> ~1%) mean elpd comparisons with this model are shaky.
# loo is not used to compare models here (one model per species), so this is a diagnostic of
# influential points rather than a gate.
loo_check = map_dfr(season_models, function(fit) {
  k = loo::pareto_k_values(fit$criteria$loo)
  tibble(n_obs = length(k),
         n_k_gt_0.7 = sum(k > 0.7),
         pct_k_gt_0.7 = round(100 * mean(k > 0.7), 2),
         max_k = max(k))
}, .id = "taxon_capture")

loo_check

```

## Posterior predictive checks by stage
```{r}
#| fig-height: 14
#| fig-width: 10

# simulate replicate datasets from the posterior and compare summary statistics with the
# observed data, separately per stage. the two statistics map onto the two model parts:
#   prop_zero    share of Bd-negative swabs -> the hurdle (hu) part
#   mean_log_pos mean log load among positives -> the lognormal (mu) part
#   sd_log_pos   spread of log load among positives -> sigma
# the observed value (dark line) should sit inside the histogram of replicated values.
# random effects are included (the default), so these check fit to the observed groups.
prop_zero = function(y) mean(y == 0)
mean_log_pos = function(y) mean(log(y[y > 0]))
sd_log_pos = function(y) sd(log(y[y > 0]))

ppc_stage = function(fit, spp) {
  stats = list(prop_zero = prop_zero, mean_log_pos = mean_log_pos, sd_log_pos = sd_log_pos)
  plots = imap(stats, function(f, nm) {
    pp_check(fit, type = "stat_grouped", stat = f, group = "life_stage_simple", ndraws = 500) +
      labs(title = if (nm == "prop_zero") str_to_sentence(gsub("_", " ", spp)) else NULL,
           subtitle = nm) +
      theme(legend.position = "none")
  })
  wrap_plots(plots, nrow = 1)
}

imap(season_models, ppc_stage) %>%
  wrap_plots(ncol = 1)

```

## Seasonal posterior predictive check
```{r}
#| fig-height: 10
#| fig-width: 12

# the key check for a seasonal model: do the fitted stage curves follow the observed data
# through the season? observed prevalence and mean log load (among positives) per 2-week period
# and stage are plotted as points over the 50% / 95% intervals of the same summaries computed
# from replicated datasets. points consistently outside the intervals in some period mean the
# k = 5 smooth (or the random effects) misses a seasonal feature there.
# periods are kept only when the observed summary is reasonably precise (>= 5 swabs for
# prevalence, >= 3 positives for load, as in the screen).
min_n_period = 5
min_pos_period = 3

season_ppc = function(fit, ndraws = 200) {
  d = fit$data %>%
    mutate(doy = round(season_m * 30.44 + 182),
           period = floor((doy - 1) / 14),
           grp = paste(life_stage_simple, period, sep = "|"),
           # one factor fixes the group order for rowsum(), table() and arrange() alike
           grp = factor(grp, levels = sort(unique(grp))))

  yrep = posterior_predict(fit, ndraws = ndraws)   # draws x observations
  pos = t(yrep > 0)                                # observations x draws
  logy = t(ifelse(yrep > 0, log(yrep), 0))

  # rowsum() sums rows within each group: (groups x draws) matrices of counts and sums
  n_grp = as.vector(table(d$grp))
  n_pos = rowsum(pos * 1, d$grp)
  sum_log = rowsum(logy, d$grp)

  prev_rep = n_pos / n_grp
  load_rep = sum_log / n_pos       # NaN where a replicate has no positives in that group

  q = function(m) {
    t(apply(m, 1, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE))
  }

  obs = d %>%
    group_by(grp, life_stage_simple, period) %>%
    summarise(n = n(),
              n_pos_obs = sum(bd_load_co100_density > 0),
              prev_obs = mean(bd_load_co100_density > 0),
              load_obs = if (n_pos_obs > 0) mean(log(bd_load_co100_density[bd_load_co100_density > 0])) else NA_real_,
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(grp)

  bind_rows(
    bind_cols(obs, as_tibble(q(prev_rep), .name_repair = ~ c("l95", "l50", "med", "u50", "u95"))) %>%
      filter(n >= min_n_period) %>%
      mutate(metric = "prevalence", observed = prev_obs),
    bind_cols(obs, as_tibble(q(load_rep), .name_repair = ~ c("l95", "l50", "med", "u50", "u95"))) %>%
      filter(n_pos_obs >= min_pos_period) %>%
      mutate(metric = "log load (positives)", observed = load_obs)
  ) %>%
    mutate(period_mid_doy = period * 14 + 7.5)
}

season_ppc_all = map_dfr(season_models, season_ppc, .id = "taxon_capture")

plot_season_ppc = function(ppc, metric_name) {
  ppc %>%
    filter(metric == metric_name) %>%
    mutate(date = as.Date(period_mid_doy - 1, origin = "2001-01-01"),
           species = str_to_sentence(gsub("_", " ", taxon_capture))) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = date, color = life_stage_simple, fill = life_stage_simple)) +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = l95, ymax = u95), linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.5,
                   position = position_dodge(width = 6)) +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = l50, ymax = u50), linewidth = 1.5, alpha = 0.6,
                   position = position_dodge(width = 6)) +
    geom_point(aes(y = observed), shape = 21, color = "black", size = 1.8,
               position = position_dodge(width = 6)) +
    facet_wrap(~ species, scales = "free") +
    scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = metric_name, color = "stage", fill = "stage",
         title = paste("Seasonal predictive check:", metric_name),
         subtitle = "points = observed per 2-week period; bars = 50% / 95% predictive intervals") +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "italic"))
}

plot_season_ppc(season_ppc_all, "prevalence")
plot_season_ppc(season_ppc_all, "log load (positives)")

# share of observed period summaries inside their 95% predictive interval (expect ~0.95;
# much lower = misfit somewhere in the season, much higher is fine with few periods)
season_ppc_all %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture, metric) %>%
  summarise(n_periods = n(),
            coverage_95 = mean(observed >= l95 & observed <= u95),
            .groups = "drop")

```

## Smooth wiggliness: posterior vs prior
```{r}
# each smooth's wiggly (penalized) part has one sd ("sds_..."): 0 = the smooth is just its
# linear part, larger = more curvature. the prior is half student_t(3, 0, 2.5). if the posterior
# looks like the prior, the data say little about curvature and the curve's shape is
# prior-driven; if it is pulled towards 0 the data prefer a near-linear seasonal trend; if it is
# well away from 0 and narrower than the prior, the data support curvature.
# the prior quantiles below are for the half-t: quantile p of |t| = 2.5 * qt((1 + p) / 2, 3)
sds_prior = tibble(prior_median = 2.5 * qt(0.75, 3),
                   prior_upper_95 = 2.5 * qt(0.975, 3))
sds_prior

sds_summary = map_dfr(season_models, function(fit) {
  posterior_summary(fit, variable = "^sds_", regex = TRUE, probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)) %>%
    as_tibble(rownames = "variable")
}, .id = "taxon_capture") %>%
  mutate(part = if_else(str_detect(variable, "^sds_hu_"), "hu", "mu"),
         # check "subadult" first: the string "adult" also matches inside it
         stage = if_else(str_detect(variable, "subadult"), "subadult", "adult"))

sds_summary %>%
  select(taxon_capture, part, stage, Q2.5, Q50, Q97.5)

ggplot(sds_summary, aes(x = Q50, xmin = Q2.5, xmax = Q97.5,
                        y = interaction(stage, part, sep = " / "))) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0, xmax = sds_prior$prior_upper_95, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "grey90") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = sds_prior$prior_median, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange() +
  facet_wrap(~ str_to_sentence(gsub("_", " ", taxon_capture))) +
  labs(x = "sds (posterior median, 95% interval)", y = NULL,
       subtitle = "grey band = prior 95% range; dashed = prior median") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "italic"))

```

## Prior sensitivity
```{r}
#| eval: false

# power-scaling sensitivity (priorsense): how much would the posterior move if the prior (or
# likelihood) were made a little stronger or weaker? "prior" values above ~0.05 flag
# prior-data conflict or a prior-dominated parameter. checked only for the parameters that
# shape the seasonal contrast: the subadult offsets, the smooths' linear parts and the smooth
# sds. slow for r. sierrae (it reweights all draws for each scaling).
# install.packages("priorsense")
library(priorsense)

season_sensitivity = imap(season_models, function(fit, spp) {
  vars = grep("^b_(hu_)?life_stage_simplesubadult$|^bs_|^sds_", variables(fit), value = TRUE)
  powerscale_sensitivity(fit, variable = vars) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    mutate(taxon_capture = spp)
}) %>%
  list_rbind()

season_sensitivity %>%
  filter(diagnosis != "-")

ggplot(season_sensitivity, aes(x = prior, y = variable, color = diagnosis)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.05, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ taxon_capture) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x = "Prior sensitivity (power-scaling)", y = NULL)

```
